findings.target: Framing and visibility of perimeter cabinetry
findings.reference_evidence: The left display cabinet spans roughly x=0.04–0.46 of the reference, while the right cabinetry begins around x=0.50; substantial portions of both are visible behind the island.
findings.render_evidence: The left cabinet is compressed into roughly x=0.49–0.76, its lower section is mostly hidden by the island, and the right cabinetry starts around x=0.72 and is heavily cropped at the right edge. A black region occupies much of the upper left.
findings.proposed_change: Use the available visual correction to adjust the camera framing and viewpoint toward the reference, bringing more of both perimeter cabinet groups into view and reducing the exposed black region.
findings.preserve: Keep the existing cabinet assemblies, their parts, and the island intact; preserve the visible distinction between upper and lower right cabinets.
findings.check_after: Compare cabinet extents, island overlap, right-edge cropping, and room coverage in the resulting render across the completed scope.
findings.uncertainty: The reference and render have different aspect ratios, and some lower cabinet contacts are obscured by the island. The exact camera adjustment cannot be determined from the images alone.

findings.reference_evidence: The cabinet wood and right countertop read as dark brown against the pale wall and lighter island top; glazing shows varied reflections.
findings.render_evidence: The visible perimeter cabinet frames and fronts appear pale tan, and the glazing reads as almost uniform pale panels. The right countertop is also much lighter than the reference.
findings.proposed_change: Carry the tonal mismatch forward for assessment after the framing correction; no separate change is proposed in this correction.
findings.preserve: Keep cabinet frames, door divisions, and hardware recognizable.
findings.check_after: Reassess wood, countertop, and glazing contrast in the corrected view.
findings.uncertainty: Lighting, exposure, and the limited visible area may contribute; the render does not establish a unique material cause.

summary: The cabinetry is present in the inventory and recognizable in the render, but its framing and visibility differ substantially from the reference. One visual correction is available; no prior findings were supplied.
